feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning in digital communications and strategy. It shows solid progression, relevant technical depth, and good alignment between brand statement and experience, though it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional narrative: the summary, title, and career progression consistently support a digital strategy leadership profile.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at one organization with promotions suggests trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels current and marketable.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond activity: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include outcomes such as engagement growth, conversion improvements, cost savings, team size, or project timelines.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap and dilute impact; consolidate for a cleaner structure.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); consider standardizing date format (“Sept.”/“Oct.”) and replacing markdown-style bold in Languages with plain text.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or sector focus.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add public-sector/member-association context to sharpen relevance: “mission-driven, advocacy-focused organizations” or “public-sector and membership organizations.”
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter value proposition focused on digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and editorial workflows that improve coordination across complex teams. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content and stakeholder-facing communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” also appears elsewhere; avoid repeating it unless adding a sharper outcome or context.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized higher-value leadership capabilities and used more consistent, resume-standard phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize wording: use parallel noun phrases and pluralize where needed (e.g., “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication”).
- Prioritize strategic, senior-level strengths over task-level items like “Web & CMS administration.”
- Consider rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Content operations & systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, swap in one more differentiator from recent work, such as “AI-enabled search strategy” or “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming or removing 2–3 items already covered in detail elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it sharper by emphasizing consulting impact, named deliverables, and 1–2 measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter lead: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented ones: “built,” “launched,” “streamlined,” “designed,” “improved.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on distinct impact areas: Drupal campaign/microsite builds; communications workflows/analytics; governance across channels; AI search initiative.
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages/templates, users, publishers, toolkits produced, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, or reduction in publishing bottlenecks.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” repeats language already used in the header and NACo role.
- AI search and microsite examples also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if channel-management bullets focused more on outcomes than scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed enterprise digital communications for NACo, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector organization.”
- Tighten the website bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast channel oversight toward impact: add metrics such as email engagement, audience growth, campaign performance, or production volume if available; otherwise shorten.
- Combine operations/analytics language: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role’s day-to-day channel management; keep this entry focused on enterprise transformation and leadership.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer project examples; keep this bullet strategic, not production-level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational ownership, cross-team coordination, and channel growth before the broader strategy/governance scope of the 2022–2024 role.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on executional leadership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial delivery and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and front-load scope: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add clearer outcome language where possible: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Sharpen operational impact: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.” 

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet; keep this version more tactical.
- Weekly video/update language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this as scaling and institutionalizing, not launching.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and implementation themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older items unless job-relevant: consider removing jQuery and possibly WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages if they are not central to recent target roles.
- Use “enterprise CMS platforms” or “public-sector web platforms” to better match the seniority shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, align wording with proven outcomes: “Drupal modernization for high-volume public-facing sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version strategic and less exhaustive.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

- Put the most senior/impact-oriented items first: strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, optimization; tools last.
- Tighten phrasing: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboarding” for clearer business value.
- If accurate, add one stronger outcome-oriented term such as “measurement frameworks” or “insight-driven optimization” to signal applied impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” list in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating every platform here if they already appear elsewhere; Topline Skills should summarize, Technical + IT should inventory.

items.title: University of Virginia

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should emphasize depth/order rather than read as a generic tool dump.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding light proficiency context: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, sharpen toward impact: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep formatting simple and consistent with other technical lists; avoid overloading this line with descriptors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this section more tool-specific while leaving strategic framing in Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus the seniority of the CV unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer, higher-signal tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/outcome cues instead of only tools, e.g. **Front-end development for Drupal microsites and enterprise web properties • API integrations • Tag management and deployment automation**
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless paired with older tech elsewhere; **HTML, CSS, JavaScript** is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Keep the detailed tool list here and shorten/remove the duplicate topline phrasing.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics/optimization; keep it here only if positioned as implementation, not reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so tighten and frame around business use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Work Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If true, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “used to build editorial workflows, intake systems, approvals, and cross-team coordination”
- Consider trimming weaker/older tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most aligned with recent work (Airtable, Power Automate, Jira/Asana, Slack/Teams)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are adjacent in meaning—listing all four may feel padded unless all were used meaningfully.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership, but this item is too bare and misses the scale/enterprise context shown in recent roles. It should signal platform depth without repeating email-channel claims already covered in work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if all three were used directly; otherwise remove any tool with limited exposure.
- If accurate, add light qualifiers for level/scope: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member communications/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter and campaign delivery)**
- Keep it platform-focused; avoid adding outcomes here unless you can tie them directly to system ownership or implementation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; don’t restate audience size or email volume here.
- “Engagement” may blur with analytics and social; “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” is clearer and more specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” and team-building contributions without repeating website/video points covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination and publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics or metrics if available: event audience size, video cadence, traffic/email growth, or production volume.
- Clarify supervision: “provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” → “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Website modernization is covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 role; keep this to “supported a website refresh.”
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Add a second sentence focused on measurable media impact if available: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs: multimedia assets, web stories, interviews, or program communications.
- If possible, quantify scope: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audience/download growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this item centered on innovation/research support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
